newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE shippers set to lift rates on Iran cargo.
newsitem.headline: UAE shippers set to lift rates on Iran cargo.

text.p: Shipping lines operating from Dubai to the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas are looking into increasing freight rates to cover added stevedoring charges levied by Iran, Khaleej Times reported on Friday.
"A cost recovery surcharge of around $21 to $25 per container may be slapped on the prevailing rate between Dubai and Bandar Abbas," the newspaper quoted shipping executives as saying.
They said the proposed surcharge would be levied to cover a 300 percent increase in stevedoring charges that Iran had started collecting from May 22.

"The charges for dicharging and loading a TEU (20-foot container) was being increased to 95,000 rials ($31.6) from the prevailing 30,000 rials," representatives of shipping lines were quoted as saying.
"For a 40-foot container it was being raised to 110,000 rials from 35,000 rials," they said.
"We have been given no choice but to accept the increased rates as we have been told that if we do not accept they will refuse to handle our cargo," one representative said.
Iranian port officials were not immediately available for comment.
The surcharge would be the second blow this week to traders and shippers operating on the Dubai-Bandar Abbas route following a move by Tehran to halt cross-border transit trade to Afghanistan.

Dubai, one of the United Arab Emirates seven emirates, is a source of many of the electronic and household goods imported by Afghanistan. The goods reach Afghanistan via Iran across the Gulf from Dubai.

Traders said earlier about 80 Dubai-based companies had over 1,000 containers stranded at the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas since Iran -- apparently angered by the Afghan Islamic militia's closure of its embassy in Kabul-- closed the transit trade through the Afghan border city of Islam Qila.
Khaleej Times said shipping lines had suspended bookings for cargo destined for Afghanistan via Iran and that containers were piling up at Dubai ports.
